sections.body: Small-batch candles, mists and oils, poured in coconut-soy wax and blended without phthalates.
sections.imageAlt: A lit pillar candle glowing inside a wooden lantern

sections.label: Pinned story
sections.heading: How a candle is made here

steps.title: Blended by nose
steps.body: Each fragrance starts as forty small trials. We keep the one that still smells good on the third evening.
steps.alt: Glass droppers and amber vials of fragrance oil

steps.title: Poured at 62°C
steps.body: Coconut-soy wax is poured slowly at a low temperature, so the scent binds to the wax instead of burning off.
steps.alt: Melted wax being poured from a pot into a glass vessel with a wick

steps.title: Cured for two weeks
steps.body: Candles rest by the studio window for fourteen days. The scent throw roughly doubles in that time.
steps.alt: Finished pillar candles resting on a windowsill

steps.title: Burned clean for sixty hours
steps.body: A cotton wick sized to the vessel gives an even melt pool and no soot on the glass.
steps.alt: Tealights burning beside amber bottles of fragrance oil

sections.label: Stacking cards
sections.heading: Four ingredients we keep returning to

cards.name: Damask rose
cards.body: Steam-distilled from petals picked before nine in the morning, when the oil is richest.

cards.name: Atlas cedar
cards.body: Dry and pencil-shaving clean. It anchors the brighter notes so they last into the evening.

cards.name: Neroli
cards.body: From bitter-orange blossom. Honeyed at first, then green and slightly bitter.

cards.name: Vetiver
cards.body: An earthy root oil that smells like rain on warm ground. A drop goes a long way.
